what: Bayesian Forecasting with Large Vector Autoregressions
title: Bayesian Forecasting with Large Vector Autoregressions
text: R package Bayesian Forecasting Large Vector Autoregressions Provides fast efficient procedures Bayesian estimation forecasting using state---art Vector Autoregressions. package includes model proposed Chan (2020), , Bayesian Vector Autoregression Minnesota priors flexible structure error term specification. latter includes: conditional multivariate normal Student’s t distributions, well homoskedastic heteroskedastic specifications common volatility modelled centred non-centred Stochastic Volatility. Additionally, package facilitates predictive analyses using density forecasting forecast-error variance decompositions. complemented simple workflows, useful plots summary functions, comprehensive documentation. ‘bvars’ package aligns R packages ‘bsvars’ Woźniak (2024), ‘bsvarSIGNs’ Wang & Woźniak (2025), ‘bpvars’ Woźniak (2025) regarding objects, workflows, code structure, constitute integrated toolset.

title: Bayesian Forecasting with Large Vector Autoregressions
text: bvars package includes state---art Vector Autoregressive models Minnesota priors flexible structure error term specification. model equations : dependent variable matrix Y, lagged dependent variable matrix X, error term E, autoregressive parameter matrix , error term covariance matrix S, diagonal matrix O allowing heteroskedasticity non-normality error term. error terms feature zero-mean matrix-variate normal distribution row-specific covariance matrix S column-specific diagonal covariance matrix O order T. parameters S follow matrix-variate normal inverse Wishart prior featuring characteristics Minnesota priors. conditional multivariate normal Student’s t distributions, homoskedastic heteroskedastic specifications common volatility modelled centred non-centred stochastic volatility.
code: Y = A X + E          (VAR equation)    E | X ~ MN(0, O, S)      (error term normality)

what: Start your Bayesian analysis of data
title: Bayesian Forecasting with Large Vector Autoregressions
text: beginnings easy ABC: bvars package supports simplified workflow using |> pipe: Now, ’re ready analyse model forecasts!
code: library(bvars)                                          # load the package  spec = specify_bvar$new(                                # specify the model   us_macro_chan,                                        # data   p = 4,                                                # number of lags   common_volatility = "ncSV",                           # heteroskedasticity   distribution = "t",                                   # Student t error term   stationary = rep(TRUE, ncol(us_macro_chan))           # Minnesota prior spec )  burn = estimate(spec, S = 10000)                        # run the burn-in post = estimate(burn, S = 10000)                        # estimate the model summary(fore)                                           # estimation summary  fore = forecast(                                        # forecast the model    post,                                                 # estimation output   horizon = 6                                           # forecast horizon )  plot(fore)                                              # plot the forecasts summary(fore)                                           # forecast summary forecasts  fevd = compute_variance_decompositions(           post, horizon = 6)                            # compute variance decompositions plot(fevd)                                              # plot variance decompositions us_macro_chan |>                                        # data   specify_bvar$new(p = 4) |>                            # specify the model   estimate(S = 10000) |>                                # run the burn-in   estimate(S = 10000) -> post                           # estimate the model  post |> forecast(horizon = 6) |> plot()                 # forecasting post |> compute_variance_decompositions(horizon = 6) |> plot()
